title: C# and the .NET Platform
learningObjectives: Identify the responsibilities of the C# compiler.
Explain the role of the .NET SDK and CLI.
Distinguish build-time compilation from runtime execution.
Describe the purpose of the .NET runtime and base class libraries.
Recognize target framework and language-version compatibility.

understand.concept: A typical .NET C# project uses the .NET SDK to restore dependencies and build source files. The C# compiler converts source into intermediate language and metadata in an assembly. A compatible .NET runtime loads and executes the application, using runtime services and libraries. The project target framework identifies the API/runtime family the application targets.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the toolchain helps diagnose missing SDKs, incompatible target frameworks, compiler errors, runtime errors and dependency problems.
understand.analogy: The SDK is a workshop containing build tools, the compiler transforms source into a packaged set of instructions, and the runtime provides services needed to execute them.
understand.analogyLimit: The process is more complex than one transformation. Build targets, analyzers, source generators, package restore, JIT or ahead-of-time compilation may participate depending on project configuration.

explain.narrative:
## The main components

- .NET SDK: project templates, CLI commands, MSBuild and compiler tooling.
- C# compiler: checks C# source and emits assemblies.
- Intermediate Language (IL): an instruction representation stored in assemblies.
- .NET runtime: loads and executes compatible assemblies and provides services such as garbage collection and exception handling.
- Base Class Library: reusable APIs for strings, collections, files, networking and more.

## Build and run

`dotnet build` restores required packages when needed and compiles the project. `dotnet run` builds and launches a project. A successful build does not guarantee correct runtime behaviour; tests and execution checks are also required.

## Target frameworks and language versions

A target framework moniker (TFM), such as `net10.0`, selects the .NET API target. The SDK normally selects a compatible default C# language version. Do not force a language version newer than the target framework supports.
